stories.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei resumes Pentagon talks to resolve AI safety standoff
key_facts: Dario Amodei has resumed discussions with Emil Michael, under-secretary of defense for research and engineering, to hammer out a new contract governing Pentagon access to Anthropic's AI
Talks had broken down after Anthropic demanded assurances its AI would not be used for mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous weapons deployment
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth subsequently declared Anthropic a 'supply chain risk to national security', a designation previously reserved for foreign adversaries like Huawei
If both sides reach a new agreement, the military could resume using Anthropic's AI and the supply-chain risk designation could be lifted
Anthropic investors including Amazon, Google, and Salesforce Ventures have pushed to de-escalate the clash, per Reuters reporting on March 4
Bloomberg Law reported the renewed talks on March 5, citing Financial Times reporting

stories.headline: Donald Knuth publishes 'Claude's Cycles' after AI solves his open graph theory conjecture
key_facts: Donald Knuth published a paper titled 'Claude's Cycles' describing how Claude Opus 4.6 solved a directed graph decomposition conjecture he had been working on for weeks
The problem involved decomposing a directed graph with m³ vertices into three Hamiltonian cycles of length m³ for all odd m > 2, earmarked for a future volume of The Art of Computer Programming
Claude completed 31 guided explorations over roughly one hour, guided by Knuth's colleague Filip Stappers, independently reformulating the problem as a Cayley digraph
The solution involved a 'serpentine' pattern corresponding to the classical modular m-ary Gray code; Knuth wrote the formal proof himself from Claude's construction
Knuth opened the paper with 'Shock! Shock!' and wrote: 'It seems I'll have to revise my opinions about generative AI one of these days'
The post sharing the paper accumulated over 635,000 views and 6,000 likes within hours; even-dimension case remains unsolved

stories.headline: Microsoft releases Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B, open-weight multimodal model rivaling systems 10x its size
key_facts: Microsoft released Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B on March 4, a 15-billion-parameter open-weight multimodal reasoning model available on HuggingFace, GitHub, and Microsoft Foundry
Combines SigLIP-2 image encoder with Phi-4 Reasoning using a mid-fusion architecture that processes both images and text
Features three thinking modes — hybrid (default, model decides), think (forced reasoning chain), and nothink (direct output) — allowing developers to control reasoning depth
Competitive with models requiring 10x or more compute; excels at math and science reasoning, chart interpretation, document reading, and GUI understanding
Primarily trained on open-source data with multistep curation process; released under a permissive license
Part of Microsoft's campaign to prove carefully engineered small models can compete with much larger AI systems

Rival Anthropic has followed a similar trajectory, climbing to roughly $9 billion in annualized revenue

Plan targets 'decisive breakthroughs in key core technologies' including AI, quantum computing, humanoid robots, advanced chips, and space technology
A separate state-planning body report asserted China now leads the world in AI research and development
Beijing aims to 'seize the commanding heights of science and technological development' per the plan's language

stories.headline: Evo 2 genome foundation model published in Nature — 40B parameters trained on all domains of life
key_facts: Evo 2, a 40-billion-parameter DNA foundation model trained on over 9 trillion nucleotides spanning all three domains of life, published in Nature on March 4, 2026
Built by Arc Institute with collaborators from Stanford, UCSF, UC Berkeley, NVIDIA, Goodfire, and University of Washington
Model predicts functional properties from genomic sequences and provides generative capabilities for designing novel biological sequences
Successfully designed functional bacteriophages — the first AI-designed and experimentally validated organisms — with potential to treat antibiotic-resistant bacteria
Uses frontier StripedHyena2 architecture with 1 megabase context length enabling near-linear scaling of compute and memory
Fully open-source and available on HuggingFace and GitHub; Nature cover featured headline: 'AI can write genomes — how long until it creates synthetic life?'

AI6 will power Tesla's Full Self-Driving autonomous system, the Optimus humanoid robot, and internal AI data centers

stories.headline: Vertiv and Generate Capital launch 'Bring Your Own Power & Cooling' model for data centers
key_facts: Vertiv and Generate Capital announced a strategic collaboration to deliver complete Bring Your Own Power & Cooling (BYOP&C) solutions for US data centers
The model combines Vertiv's power and cooling infrastructure with Generate's financing, asset ownership, and operational expertise
Initial deployments target North American markets with constrained grid access, using reciprocating engines, turbines, fuel cells, battery storage, and alternative energy
The collaboration addresses two key constraints: grid connection delays and high upfront infrastructure capital requirements
Generate's financing model reduces or eliminates upfront customer infrastructure investment while preserving future grid-connection optionality
Vertiv will provide modular, fully converged building blocks designed to shorten design cycles and standardize deployment

stories.headline: UK GPU datacenter demonstrates 40% AI power reduction on demand in National Grid trial
key_facts: A London GPU datacenter operated by Nebius achieved a 40% reduction in AI power consumption during a five-day trial in December 2025, results published March 4
The trial involved Nebius, National Grid, Emerald AI, and EPRI's Datacenter Flexible Load Initiative
Over 200 simulated grid event notifications were tested across a 130 kW compute cluster running Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs
Power flexibility was achieved by pausing or deprioritizing GPU jobs and shifting workloads, not by powering down equipment
AI training workloads including GPT, Llama, and Qwen models proved suitable due to natural checkpoint intervals where processing can pause
The trial achieved 100% compliance with all requested power reduction targets and ramp rates
National Grid Partners president Steve Smith said 'High-performance datacenters don't have to place additional strain on the grid'

stories.headline: Seven tech giants sign White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge to self-fund data center power
key_facts: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle, and xAI signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge at the White House on March 4
Companies committed to build, bring, or buy new generation resources and cover all power delivery infrastructure upgrades for their data centers
Signatories will negotiate new separate rate structures with utilities and state governments wherever they build data centers
Companies agreed to pay these rates whether or not they use the electricity, ensuring costs are not passed to American households
The pledge includes commitments to hire and train workers from communities where data centers operate
Companies will coordinate with grid operators to make backup generation resources available, contributing to grid reliability
The signing took place in the Indian Treaty Room of the Eisenhower Executive Office Building

stories.headline: NTSB finds Waymo remote operator told robotaxi to illegally pass stopped school bus in Austin
key_facts: The NTSB published a preliminary report on a January 12, 2026 incident where a Waymo robotaxi illegally passed a stopped school bus in Austin, Texas
The autonomous system functioned correctly by stopping and asking its remote human operator 'Is this a school bus with active signals?' — the operator responded 'No' and the vehicle proceeded
The illegal pass prompted five other human-driven vehicles to follow suit, compounding the safety risk for students
Waymo issued a voluntary software recall on 3,000 vehicles to address school bus detection issues
Austin ISD has asked Waymo to cease operations during morning and afternoon school hours when students use buses
Under Texas Transportation Code Section 545.066, drivers must remain stopped until a school bus deactivates its signals

stories.headline: Japan's Space One Kairos rocket fails for third consecutive time, self-destructs 69 seconds after liftoff
key_facts: Space One's Kairos No. 3 rocket self-destructed 68.8 seconds after liftoff from Spaceport Kii on March 5, after the flight termination system activated
About 70 seconds after liftoff an energetic event became visible in the rocket's plume with several fragments including one large tumbling piece
The first-stage engine burn had carried the 18-meter, 23-ton solid-fuel rocket to an altitude of about 29 kilometers before termination
The rocket was carrying five experimental satellites from Japanese companies and the Taiwan Space Agency
Space One suggested a malfunction in the safety system that automatically determines flight termination may have occurred
This was the third consecutive failure: Kairos No. 1 exploded after liftoff in March 2024, No. 2 self-destructed in December 2024
Reuters reported the failure 'leaves Japan without commercial launch capability,' highlighting reliance on American rockets amid space-security concerns

stories.headline: Iran war Day 6: Senate blocks war powers resolution 53-47 as strikes expand inland
key_facts: US Senate voted 53-47 to block the Iran War Powers Resolution that would have required Trump to seek congressional approval before continuing military action
Republican Sen. Rand Paul broke with his party to support the resolution; Democratic Sen. John Fetterman voted against it

US death toll rose to six soldiers killed in Iranian retaliatory strikes; Iranian death toll surpassed 1,045 since Saturday

stories.headline: NATO intercepts Iranian ballistic missile headed toward Turkey, first strike on alliance territory
key_facts: NATO air defense systems destroyed an Iranian ballistic missile heading into Turkish airspace after passing over Iraqi and Syrian airspace
This marks the first time an Iranian missile has been fired toward NATO territory in the current conflict
Debris from the intercepting missile fell in the Dortyol district of Hatay province near the Syrian border; no casualties reported
A Turkish official said the missile was aimed at a base in Greek Cyprus but veered off course
Turkey could potentially invoke NATO's Article 4 after the airspace breach, a step that could lead to Article 5 collective defense obligations
President Erdogan said Turkey was 'taking all the necessary precautions' in consultation with NATO allies
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Turkey's foreign minister Hakan Fidan pledging Washington's full support and calling the attacks on Turkey's sovereignty 'unacceptable'

stories.headline: EU asylum agency warns Iran turmoil could trigger refugee movements of 'unprecedented magnitude'
key_facts: The European Union Agency for Asylum (EUAA) warned that destabilization of Iran could generate refugee movements of 'unprecedented magnitude' given its population of approximately 90 million
EU asylum applications dropped nearly 20% in 2025 to around 822,000 across EU+ states, largely driven by fewer applications from Syrians after Assad's ouster
EU interior ministers are scheduled to discuss the issue at a Brussels meeting on Thursday March 6
The European Commission said it was 'enhancing preparedness through closer monitoring' and reinforcing cooperation with UN agencies
The EUAA report was written before the US-Israel war with Iran began, identifying Iran as a 'potential flashpoint'

stories.headline: Canada and Australia call for Iran war de-escalation while insisting Tehran must never acquire nuclear weapons
key_facts: Canadian PM Mark Carney and Australian PM Anthony Albanese jointly called for de-escalation of the Iran war during a meeting in Canberra
Carney said: 'We want to see a broader de-escalation of these hostilities with a broader group of countries than just the direct belligerents involved'
Albanese said: 'I want to see the possibility of Iran getting a nuclear weapon removed once and for all'
Carney stated the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council should become involved in the de-escalation process, praising the GCC countries for 'showing tremendous restraint'
Carney separately described Canada's support for the US-Israeli strikes as 'not a blank cheque'
The joint statement follows growing international pressure for a diplomatic off-ramp as the conflict enters its sixth day

stories.headline: ARPA-H awards $22M to study Transposon's TPN-101 for extending healthy aging under PROSPR program
key_facts: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) awarded up to $22 million to Transposon Therapeutics to study TPN-101 for healthy aging
The award is under the PROSPR (Proactive Solutions for Prolonging Resilience) program aimed at extending healthspan
TPN-101 is a first-in-class LINE-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitor that reduces activation of innate immunity and its associated inflammatory and senescence processes
Transposon is advancing TPN-101 in late-stage clinical trials for progressive supranuclear palsy, ALS, and Alzheimer's disease
No FDA-approved therapies currently exist to extend healthspan or slow aging
CEO Dennis Podlesak called the award 'a transformative opportunity to advance TPN-101 into an entirely new therapeutic category that targets the underlying causes of age-related disease'

stories.headline: NEJM publishes first evidence of disease modification in Dravet syndrome with Stoke/Biogen's zorevunersen
key_facts: Results from Phase 1/2a and open-label extension studies of zorevunersen were published in the New England Journal of Medicine on March 5
The studies demonstrate for the first time the potential for disease modification in Dravet syndrome, a severe genetic neurodevelopmental disease
Patients receiving 70mg doses showed motor seizure reduction of nearly 85% at three months and 73% at six months
Extension study patients experienced seizure reduction ranging from 58% to 90% over 20 months
Treatment showed improvements in communication, motor skills, socialization, daily living, and quality of life beyond just seizure control
Zorevunersen is an antisense oligonucleotide designed to increase functional NaV1.1 protein production from the unaffected SCN1A gene
Developed by Stoke Therapeutics (Nasdaq: STOK) and Biogen (Nasdaq: BIIB); a global Phase 3 EMPEROR study is enrolling approximately 150 patients
